what: The section’s top edge rises like a window frame, revealing a full-bleed photo stuck to the screen (the photo stays put, only the frame rises). Over the next 150vh of scrolling, the photo settles from 1.3× at 5% down to its normal size and position, and when the section content rising at the end covers the photo, the photo is pushed up 30% by progress²
ease: none (tied to scroll) · push-out is progress²

options.lift: Distance pushed up when covered (%), default 30
options.hold: Length of the sinking section (vh), default 150 — this much empty space is left behind the photo
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Panel stuck to the screen (first child of the section) — the part applies sticky, 100vh and −100vh upward
options.[data-fx-part=photo]: Photo that grows then settles inside panel
options.[data-fx-part=spacer]: (if present) slot for the sinking segment — if absent, the parts are built after the panel

use: …section content (rises up covering the photo)…

from.where: index.html five .scene (scene-kv sticky −100vh · scene-kv-margin 150vh · scale(1.3 − tb×.3) · translateY(5% − tb×5% − bt²×30%))

note: Section content goes after the photo panel (DOM order) and needs a painted background to cover the photos. On phones (767px and below) the original uses only scale with no vertical offset, but the part applies both regardless of width — to turn it off on phones use drift: 0; lift: 0
